text:
rachel: I opened a PR to add a tenant-isolation section to Dedicated provisioning. It adds an "isolation decorator" pattern, a short Go SDK snippet for tagging requests with tenant metadata, and guidance for when to use tenant-level reserved pools vs shared pools. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/678
kevin: Nice. Can you paste the Go snippet here? want to confirm the error handling style matches our SDK conventions.
priya: Also can we add a short note about audit logs and KMS scoping for isolated tenants? Ops asked for that.
rachel: Go snippet (compact):
```go
client := dedicated.NewClient(os.Getenv("REDWOOD_KEY"))
ctx := context.Background()
req := &dedicated.ReserveRequest{PoolName:"tenant-42-prod",GPUs:2,Annotations:map[string]string{"tenant":"tenant-42","env":"prod"}}
pool, err := client.ReservePool(ctx, req)
if err != nil {
    if errors.Is(err, dedicated.ErrPreempted) {
        // fallback to smaller variant or hosted route
        log.Println("preempted, falling back")
    } else {
        return err
    }
}
```
kevin: That looks good. Two doc nits: 1) add table mapping isolation level -> billing -> SLA; 2) include which headers the tenant annotation maps to in the routing layer.
priya: Re: audit logs  add callout: "For Private deployments rebind KMS and ensure tenant service accounts are in the audit allowlist."
